title: Medicine - Ms Eleanor Bennet
writingTask:
Using the information given in the case notes, write a letter of referral to Dr Banerjee, consultant cardiologist. In your letter, briefly outline Ms Bennet's history and treatment so far, requesting advice and a review of her medication. Address your letter to Dr James Banerjee, Consultant Cardiologist, Sanditon City Hospital, Sanditon.

In your answer:
- Expand the relevant notes into complete sentences
- Do not use note form
- Use letter format

The body of the letter should be approximately 180–200 words.
caseNotes: Patient is Eleanor Bennet, DOB 06 Dec 1975 (45 years old)
Address: 32 Station Road, Oakville
Commercial lawyer with frequent international travel
Divorced, with two daughters aged 18 and 16
Children live mainly with their father (custody currently contested); patient reports extreme stress about the quality of the father's childcare
Since 2019, alcohol intake has increased from 10 to 40 units per week
Smokes 20 cigarettes a day
BMI 29 (overweight); little exercise (gym once a month)
Father died aged 53 of heart disease
Older brother has mental health problems, with two suicide attempts in the last 12 months
08 Feb 2021, 0800 hrs: heart attack at the airport after a long-haul flight, with pain in the jaw, nausea and shortness of breath
Defibrillator applied by a first-aider
08 Feb 2021, 0915 hrs: emergency hospital admission to Oakville General Hospital
Balloon-expandable stent applied via the groin (arm access tried initially, but the artery was too small)
Discharged 15 Feb 2021, with 4 weeks off work and a gradual return to work
Mother moved in to provide care; patient reports increased stress due to a poor relationship with her mother
Discharge medication: Captopril 50mg twice daily
Discharge medication: Atorvastatin 80mg daily
Referred for cardiac rehabilitation sessions, but has not attended
Counselling given regarding lifestyle changes
15 May 2021: presenting with side effects of captopril – dizziness and light-headedness, headaches, and episodes of diarrhoea
Patient reports increased stress from the medication side effects
Patient requests discontinuation of captopril due to the side effects, and is reluctant to start new medications
Plan noted in GP's own record: referral to cardiologist regarding medication review and ways to encourage lifestyle changes
Ms Bennet was fitted with a Holter monitor, to be removed at her appointment on 22 May 2021.
candidateLetter:
Dr James Banerjee
Consultant Cardiologist
Sanditon City Hospital
Sanditon

15 May 2021

Dear Dr Banerjee,
Re: Ms Eleanor Bennet, DOB: 6 December 1975

I am writing to request a medication review for Ms Eleanor Bennet, who has developed captopril side effects following a myocardial infarction.

Today, Ms Bennet presented with dizziness, light-headedness, headaches and intermittent diarrhoea attributed to captopril. She requests its discontinuation and is reluctant to start new medications.

On 8 February 2021, Ms Bennet had a myocardial infarction after a long-haul flight. A first-aider applied a defibrillator. She underwent stent insertion at Oakville General Hospital and was discharged on 15 February 2021 taking captopril, 50 mg twice daily and atorvastatin, 80 mg daily. She received lifestyle counselling and was referred for cardiac rehabilitation, which she has not attended.

Ms Bennet smokes twenty cigarettes daily, and her alcohol intake has increased from ten to forty units weekly since 2019. Her body mass index is 29 kg/m², and she exercises monthly. She reports extreme stress about the care her daughters receive from their father. Living with her mother, with whom she has a poor relationship, has increased her stress. Her father died of heart disease at age fifty-three.

I would be grateful if you could advise on encouraging lifestyle changes.

Should there be any queries, kindly do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor
